01 Antidepressants · class card

SNRIs

serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors · venlafaxine · desvenlafaxine · duloxetine · levomilnacipran · milnacipran

Key point
  • Serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs): serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake blockade dose-dependent ↑ blood pressure
  • Most common SNRI adverse effect: dose-dependent ↑ blood pressure
  • Venlafaxine: typically avoided in hypertension
  • SNRI discontinuation syndrome
  • Onset: within days of an abrupt stop
  • Highest risk: venlafaxine (short half-life)
  • Symptoms: flu-like illness; no seizures
  • Prevention: slow taper
  • Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), SNRIs: first line for generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, posttraumatic stress disorder
  • Duloxetine: also used for diabetic neuropathy, fibromyalgia
  • SNRI with a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI), linezolid, other serotonergic drugs serotonin syndrome
Drugs

Venlafaxine Effexor XR (extended release): short half-life more discontinuation symptoms

Desvenlafaxine Pristiq: active metabolite of venlafaxine

Duloxetine: efficacy and adverse effects similar to venlafaxine; also used for pain

Levomilnacipran Fetzima

Milnacipran Savella: fibromyalgia

Mechanism

Serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake blockade at the presynaptic neuron

↑ norepinephrine dose-dependent ↑ blood pressure

Abrupt stop of a short half-life drug (venlafaxine) discontinuation symptoms

Uses

Depression: alternative to SSRIs

Generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorder, social anxiety disorder: first line, with SSRIs

Posttraumatic stress disorder: first line with SSRIs

Obsessive-compulsive disorder: second-line venlafaxine

: duloxetine Line of therapy for neuropathic painFirst line: tricyclic antidepressants, gabapentinoidsOther option: duloxetine

Fibromyalgia: duloxetine, milnacipran

Chronic low back pain despite exercise and acetaminophen or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs: duloxetine may help

Adverse effects

: dose-dependent ↑ blood pressure SNRI adverse effects in clinical trialsIn practice: nausea is the most frequent adverse effectVenlafaxine extended release: nausea in 30% of patientsDuloxetine trials, most common: nausea, dry mouth, somnolence, constipation, decreased appetite, hyperhidrosisDuloxetine trials: mean systolic ↑ 0.5 mm Hg; placebo ↓ 0.6 mm Hg

Nausea: most common problem in the first 2 weeks

Other adverse effects: stimulant effects or sedation

Sexual dysfunction: as with SSRIs

: after an abrupt stop; no seizures SNRI discontinuation symptomsMnemonic: "finish"Flu-like symptomsInsomniaNauseaImbalanceSensory disturbancesHyperarousal

Serotonin syndrome: with another serotonergic drug

Other

Venlafaxine: may cause a false-positive phencyclidine (PCP) result on a standard urine drug screen

Dose-dependent hypertension↑ blood pressure, greater at higher doses; heart rate may also rise

If hypertension is present before starting, choose an antidepressant other than venlafaxine.

Discontinuation syndromeSymptoms: flu-like aches, nausea, dizziness, irritability, electric shock-like sensations
Onset: within days of an abrupt stop

Discontinuation syndrome: can mimic depressive relapse or influenza

Treatment: restart venlafaxine and taper slowly, or support if the patient declines to restart ·

If venlafaxine is to be stopped, choose a slow taper.

Serotonin syndromeFindings: typically fever, mental status changes, autonomic instability, hyperreflexia, clonus
Triggers with an SNRI include: monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI), linezolid, tramadol, triptans, ondansetron

Practice
  1. 52-year-old man with generalized anxiety disorder at a follow-up visit venlafaxine dose doubled 2 months ago; trazodone at bedtime no new drugs, salt or alcohol change BP 154/98 mm Hg, was 126/80 · HR 92/min → Venlafaxine → venlafaxine raises blood pressure in a dose-dependent way and is typically avoided in hypertension; trazodone blocks alpha-1 receptors and lowers blood pressure on standing
  2. 34-year-old woman stopped venlafaxine abruptly 2 days ago felt well for a year; ran out of pills now dizzy, nauseated, irritable, achy as if with flu T 37.0 °C · no seizures → Restart venlafaxine, then taper slowly → abrupt stops of venlafaxine, a short half-life drug, bring discontinuation symptoms within days, flu-like among them; restarting and tapering slowly treats them
  3. 29-year-old woman with generalized anxiety disorder has a pre-employment urine drug screen takes only venlafaxine; denies any drug use screen positive for phencyclidine calm, oriented · no nystagmus · BP 118/76 mm Hg → Venlafaxine cross-reactivity → venlafaxine can produce a false-positive phencyclidine result on a standard urine drug screen; she has none of the agitation or nystagmus of real use
